biome.qtcraft.desert.description: Sand and sandstone with cacti and little else.
biome.qtcraft.forest.description: Dense oaks and birches with mushrooms in the shade.
biome.qtcraft.mountains.description: High rocky peaks with snow on top.
biome.qtcraft.plains.description: Open grassland with flowers and few trees; pigs and sheep graze here.
biome.qtcraft.swamp.description: Low wet land with clay, sugar cane and, at night, fireflies.
biome.qtcraft.taiga.description: Cool spruce forest with snow on the ground.
biome.qtcraft.tundra.description: Cold flat land under snow; its water freezes.
block.qtcraft.bedrock.description: The unbreakable floor of the world.
block.qtcraft.birch_leaves.description: Leaves decay a few at a time once no log is near. They sometimes drop a sapling.
block.qtcraft.birch_log.description: Wood of the birch. Four planks each; burns in the furnace into charcoal.
block.qtcraft.birch_planks.description: Building wood; any planks fit recipes that ask for planks.
block.qtcraft.birch_sapling.description: Plant it on grass or earth and it grows into a birch after a while.
block.qtcraft.black_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.blue_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.bricks.description: Fired clay, a sturdy building block.
block.qtcraft.brown_mushroom.description: Grows in the shade of forests and swamps.
block.qtcraft.cactus.description: Grows in deserts. Smelted, it gives green dye.
block.qtcraft.chest.description: Stores {qtcraft:chest.slots} stacks. Its contents drop when it is broken.
block.qtcraft.clay.description: Found under shallow water. Four clay make an unfired lamp shell; bricks come from the furnace.
block.qtcraft.coal_ore.description: The most common ore; drops coal, the best early fuel.
block.qtcraft.cobblestone.description: What stone becomes when mined. Material for stone tools and the furnace.
block.qtcraft.cornflower.description: A blue flower of the plains; gives blue dye.
block.qtcraft.crafting_table.description: Opens the 3 × 3 crafting grid that bigger recipes need.
block.qtcraft.dandelion.description: A yellow flower; gives yellow dye.
block.qtcraft.diamond_ore.description: Rare and deep. Needs a pickaxe of level {qtcraft:diamond_ore.toolLevel} or better.
block.qtcraft.furnace.description: Smelts ores, sand, clay and food while fuel burns: input on top, fuel below, result on the right.
block.qtcraft.glass.description: Clear block made from sand in the furnace.
block.qtcraft.glass_pane.description: A thin glass wall that connects to its neighbours.
block.qtcraft.gold_ore.description: Deep ore that needs a pickaxe of level {qtcraft:gold_ore.toolLevel}; smelts into gold ingots.
block.qtcraft.grass_block.description: Earth covered with grass, the surface of most land.
block.qtcraft.gravel.description: Loose stones that fall when nothing holds them.
block.qtcraft.green_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.ice.description: Covers the water of cold biomes.
block.qtcraft.iron_ore.description: Needs a pickaxe of level {qtcraft:iron_ore.toolLevel} or better. Smelt it into iron for better tools, buckets and more.
block.qtcraft.ladder.description: Hang it on a wall and climb up by walking into it or jumping; sneak to hold on.
block.qtcraft.lava.description: Hot liquid that glows, burns items and hurts. Next to water it turns into obsidian or cobblestone.
block.qtcraft.mine_lamp.description: A lamp with a firefly inside: hangs from ceilings, walls or floors and glows without fuel.
block.qtcraft.oak_door.description: Two blocks tall; use it to open or close it.
block.qtcraft.oak_leaves.description: Leaves decay a few at a time once no log is near. They sometimes drop a sapling.
block.qtcraft.oak_log.description: Wood of the oak: the first thing to collect. Four planks each.
block.qtcraft.oak_planks.description: Building wood; any planks fit recipes that ask for planks.
block.qtcraft.oak_sapling.description: Plant it on grass or earth and it grows into an oak after a while.
block.qtcraft.oak_trapdoor.description: A hatch on the floor or the ceiling; use it to open or close it.
block.qtcraft.obsidian.description: Forms where water meets a lava source. Very hard; needs a pickaxe of level {qtcraft:obsidian.toolLevel}.
block.qtcraft.orange_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.poppy.description: A red flower; gives red dye.
block.qtcraft.purple_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.red_mushroom.description: Grows in the shade of forests and swamps.
block.qtcraft.red_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
block.qtcraft.sand.description: Falls when nothing holds it. Smelts into glass.
block.qtcraft.snow_block.description: Packed snow of cold mountains and tundra.
block.qtcraft.snow_layer.description: A thin cover of snow that needs a block below.
block.qtcraft.spruce_leaves.description: Leaves decay a few at a time once no log is near. They sometimes drop a sapling.
block.qtcraft.spruce_log.description: Wood of the spruce. Four planks each.
block.qtcraft.spruce_planks.description: Building wood; any planks fit recipes that ask for planks.
block.qtcraft.spruce_sapling.description: Plant it on grass, earth or snow and it grows into a spruce after a while.
block.qtcraft.stone.description: The rock of the world. Drops cobblestone; needs a pickaxe.
block.qtcraft.sugar_cane.description: Grows on sand or earth right next to water.
block.qtcraft.tall_grass.description: Covers meadows; you can build right into it.
block.qtcraft.torch.description: The simplest light. Stands on floors or hangs on walls; water washes it away.
block.qtcraft.water.description: Flows up to {qtcraft:water.flowDistance} blocks from a source; two sources make a new one. Take it with a bucket.
block.qtcraft.white_wool.description: Soft block from sheep; dye any wool with a dye to colour it.
block.qtcraft.yellow_wool.description: Wool coloured with a dye. Two wool make three carpets.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.first.text:
- Break a few logs of a tree with your hand (hold the left mouse button).
- Open the inventory (E) and turn the logs into planks, then planks into sticks and a crafting table.
- Place the crafting table and use it (right mouse button) to make a wooden pickaxe.
- Mine stone for a stone pickaxe and look for coal: coal and a stick make torches.
- Build a shelter before the night; a day lasts {day.length} s.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.first.title: The first day
chapter.qtcraft.basics.goal.text: QtCraft is a world of blocks. Collect them, build with them, craft tools, smelt ores and stay alive: creatures come out at night and hunger grows while you work.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.goal.title: What to do
chapter.qtcraft.basics.handbook.text: Press F1 at any time. Every block, item, creature and biome has a page with its values, its recipes and links to where it comes from and what it is used for. In the inventory, the furnace and chests, point at an item and press F1 or click the small ? on it.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.handbook.title: This handbook
chapter.qtcraft.building.parts.text: Many materials come as stairs, slabs, walls, fences and gates. Fences, walls and panes connect to their neighbours. Doors, trapdoors and gates open and close when used; sneak to place a block against them instead.
chapter.qtcraft.building.parts.title: Building parts
chapter.qtcraft.building.placing.text: Use the held block on a face (right mouse button) to place it next to that face. Stairs and furnaces turn by your view, slabs and stairs go high or low by where you click, torches and ladders hang on the face you click. Tall grass is replaced by what you place into it.
chapter.qtcraft.building.placing.title: Placing blocks
chapter.qtcraft.building.support.text: Torches, ladders, lamps, doors and plants need something to stand or hang on. When it goes, they break and drop. Sand and gravel fall when nothing is below them.
chapter.qtcraft.building.support.title: Support
chapter.qtcraft.controls.keys.text:
- **Mouse**: look around (click into the window first)
- **W A S D**: walk, **Space**: jump or swim up, **Shift**: sneak, **Ctrl**: sprint
- **Left mouse** or **F**: mine, attack a creature
- **Right mouse** or **R**: place, use, eat
- **Q**: throw one item, **Ctrl+Q**: the whole stack
- **1–9**, mouse wheel: choose the hotbar slot
- **E**: inventory, **T** or **Enter**: chat, **F5**: camera view, **F1**: handbook, **Esc**: menu
chapter.qtcraft.controls.keys.title: Keys and mouse
chapter.qtcraft.controls.moving.text: You walk at {player.walkSpeed} m/s, sprint at {player.sprintSpeed} m/s and sneak at {player.sneakSpeed} m/s; sneaking keeps you from falling off edges. Steps up to {player.stepHeight} m are climbed without jumping. In water you swim at {player.swimSpeed} m/s.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.moving.title: Moving
chapter.qtcraft.controls.screens.text: In the inventory, furnace and chest screens a left click picks a stack up and puts it down (merging or swapping), a right click puts down a single item. The list on the right of the inventory crafts recipes directly.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.screens.title: Screens
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.book.text: The inventory lists what you can make right now; a click crafts it. Some recipes ask for a group such as any planks or coal or charcoal: every item of the group fits.
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.book.title: Recipe list and groups
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.grid.text: The inventory has a 2 × 2 grid; a crafting table within {crafting.tableReach} m opens 3 × 3. Lay out the ingredients as the recipe shows (shaped recipes may sit anywhere in the grid and be mirrored, shapeless ones in any order) and take the result. Leaving the screen puts the grid back into the inventory.
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.grid.title: The crafting grid
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.limits.text: Near each player there are at most {mobs.hostileCap} hostile, {mobs.passiveCap} peaceful and {mobs.ambientCap} ambient creatures. Creatures farther than {mobs.despawnDistance} m from every player vanish.
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.limits.title: Limits
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.spawning.text: Creatures appear {mobs.spawnRadiusMin}–{mobs.spawnRadiusMax} m away from players: peaceful animals on grass by day, hostile ones in the dark at night and in caves at least {mobs.caveDepth} blocks below the surface. Torches and lamps keep hostile creatures away. Each page lists the blocks, biomes, time and light a creature needs.
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.spawning.title: Where creatures appear
chapter.qtcraft.death.death.text: At zero health you die. Respawn takes you back to the spawn point with full health and food. With the game rule keepInventory (on by default) you keep your items; otherwise they scatter where you died.
chapter.qtcraft.death.death.title: When you die
chapter.qtcraft.death.items.text: Items on the ground vanish after {items.despawnSeconds} s while their area is loaded. Items you throw can be picked up again after {items.thrownPickupDelay} s.
chapter.qtcraft.death.items.title: Dropped items
chapter.qtcraft.health.fighting.text: Left-click a creature within {player.attackReach} m to hit it, at most every {player.attackCooldown} s. Swords and axes deal more damage than the hand; every hit knocks the target back.
chapter.qtcraft.health.fighting.title: Fighting
chapter.qtcraft.health.health.text: You have {player.maxHealth} health points, shown as hearts. Falls deeper than {player.fallDamageThreshold} m cost one point per further metre; landing in water or on a ladder is safe. Hostile creatures, lava and starving hurt as well. After a hit you cannot be hurt for {player.hurtInvulnerability} s.
chapter.qtcraft.health.health.title: Health
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.effects.text: With at least {hunger.regenerationFood} food points you heal one health point every {hunger.regenerationInterval} s. With an empty food bar you lose one health point every {hunger.starvationInterval} s, but hunger alone never takes you below {hunger.starvationFloor}.
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.effects.title: Healing and starving
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.food.text: The food bar holds {hunger.maxFood} points. Hold food and use it (right mouse button) to eat when you are not full. Walking, sprinting, swimming, jumping, mining, fighting and being hurt make you hungry: every {hunger.exhaustionPerFood} points of exhaustion cost one food point.
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.food.title: Eating
chapter.qtcraft.mining.breaking.text: Hold the left mouse button on a block within {player.reach} m. Each hardness point takes {mining.secondsPerHardness} s by hand; the right tool divides that time by its speed. Broken blocks drop their items, which you pick up by walking over them.
chapter.qtcraft.mining.breaking.title: Breaking blocks
chapter.qtcraft.mining.tools.text: Stone and ores need a pickaxe of a certain level: wood is level {qtcraft:wooden_pickaxe.toolLevel}, stone {qtcraft:stone_pickaxe.toolLevel}, iron {qtcraft:iron_pickaxe.toolLevel}, diamond {qtcraft:diamond_pickaxe.toolLevel}. With a weaker tool or none, mining takes {mining.secondsPerHardnessWithoutTool} s per hardness point and drops nothing. Tools wear out with every block.
chapter.qtcraft.mining.tools.title: Tools and levels
chapter.qtcraft.rules.commands.text:
Open the chat with T and type a command:
- `/help`, `/save`
- `/give <item> [count]`, `/spawnitem <item> [count]`
- `/time set day|night|<seconds>`, `/time add <seconds>`
- `/summon <creature> [count]` (at most {commands.summonLimit} creatures), `/kill`, `/heal`, `/feed [points]`
- `/setblock <x> <y> <z> <block>`, `/fill <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> <block>` (at most {commands.maxFill} blocks; `~` means your position)
- `/locatebiome <biome>`
All but `/help`, `/save` and reading a game rule are cheats; single-player worlds allow them.
chapter.qtcraft.rules.commands.title: Commands
chapter.qtcraft.rules.rules.text: **keepInventory**: keep the inventory on death (chosen when creating a world). Show or change it with `/gamerule keepInventory [true|false]`.
chapter.qtcraft.rules.rules.title: Game rules
chapter.qtcraft.smelting.furnace.text: A furnace takes something to smelt on top and fuel below; the result appears on the right. It burns one fuel item at a time while it has work, and keeps working while you are away as long as its area is loaded. Breaking it drops what is inside.
chapter.qtcraft.smelting.furnace.title: Smelting
chapter.qtcraft.world.liquids.text: Water and lava flow from their sources; a bucket takes a source and pours it elsewhere. Where lava meets water it hardens into obsidian or cobblestone. Lava lights its surroundings, burns items and hurts.
chapter.qtcraft.world.liquids.title: Water and lava
chapter.qtcraft.world.time.text: A full day lasts {day.length} s. The world is generated from its seed while you explore it; only what you change is saved.
chapter.qtcraft.world.time.title: Day and night
handbook.fact.infinite: Two sources make a new one
handbook.fact.plantChance: Plants itself when its item despawns
handbook.intro: Everything the game contains, generated from the game's content data by `qtcraft-headless --export-handbook`. The same pages are in the game (F1).
handbook.ore.title: %1 veins
handbook.table.fuelsText: Machines such as the furnace burn one fuel item at a time while they have something to process. The times are at machine speed 1.
handbook.table.smeltingText: Everything machines make, with the time per item.
handbook.table.toolsText: A block that needs a tool drops its items only when mined with that kind of tool of at least its level. Higher levels mine faster and last longer.
handbook.tag.text: Recipes that ask for this group take any of its items.
handbook.title: QtCraft handbook
handbook.value.anySolidOrLiquid: Any solid block or the surface of a liquid.
handbook.value.categoryCap.ambient: all ambient creatures together: %1 per player
handbook.value.categoryCap.hostile: all hostile creatures together: %1 per player
handbook.value.categoryCap.passive: all peaceful creatures together: %1 per player
handbook.value.caves: also in caves at any time
handbook.value.everyChunk: Tried in every chunk, whatever the biome.
handbook.value.supportAttached: a solid face it hangs on
handbook.value.veins: %1 per chunk, up to %2 blocks each
handbook.world.terrainText: Every world is generated from its seed: hills and plains by biome, caves below, seas up to the sea level. The same seed always gives the same world.

item.qtcraft.charcoal.description: Burnt wood: fuel as good as coal and part of torches.
item.qtcraft.coal.description: Fuel for the furnace and part of torches.
item.qtcraft.cooked_porkchop.description: Good food that fills a lot of the food bar.
item.qtcraft.diamond.description: The hardest material, for the best tools.

item.qtcraft.diamond_sword.description: A weapon: deals more damage to creatures.
item.qtcraft.fired_lamp_shell.descriptio: Put a firefly in a bottle into it to make a mine lamp.
item.qtcraft.firefly_bottle.description: A caught firefly. It lights the mine lamp.
item.qtcraft.glass_bottle.description: Use it on a firefly at night in a swamp to catch it.
item.qtcraft.green_dye.description: Made from cactus in the furnace.
item.qtcraft.iron_ingot.description: Smelted iron for tools, buckets and more.
item.qtcraft.iron_shovel.description: Digs earth, sand and gravel faster.
item.qtcraft.iron_sword.description: A weapon: deals more damage to creatures.

item.qtcraft.orange_dye.description: Mixed from red and yellow dye.
item.qtcraft.purple_dye.description: Mixed from red and blue dye.
item.qtcraft.raw_porkchop.description: Food from pigs; cook it in the furnace for more.
item.qtcraft.stone_shovel.description: Digs earth, sand and gravel faster.
item.qtcraft.stone_sword.description: A weapon: deals more damage to creatures.
item.qtcraft.unfired_lamp_shell.descript: Clay shaped into a lamp; fire it in the furnace.

item.qtcraft.wooden_sword.description: A weapon: deals more damage to creatures.
mob.qtcraft.firefly.description: Glows over swamps at night. Catch it with an empty glass bottle.
mob.qtcraft.pig.description: Peaceful farm animal of grassy land; drops porkchops.
mob.qtcraft.sheep.description: Peaceful animal of grassy land; drops wool.
mob.qtcraft.slime.description: A bouncing blob of the caves, weak but persistent.
mob.qtcraft.zombie.description: Comes out at night and lives in caves. Chases players it sees and hits hard.
part.qtcraft.carpet.description: A thin layer of wool that needs a block below.
part.qtcraft.fence.description: Fences connect to fences, gates and full solid blocks and are too high to jump over.
part.qtcraft.fence_gate.description: A gate in a fence: use it to open or close it. Open gates let everything through.
part.qtcraft.slab.description: Half a block. The clicked half decides whether it lies low or high; a second slab on the open half makes a full double slab.
part.qtcraft.stairs.description: Stairs turn away from you when placed; place them on the upper half of a face to hang them upside down. You walk up them without jumping.
part.qtcraft.wall.description: Walls connect to each other and to full solid blocks; in straight runs they leave out the post. Nobody jumps over them.
